articles.chapeau: Les fans de GTA ont enfin pu découvrir le sixième volet de la saga jeudi 19 novembre. Parmi les nouveautés : l’arrivée d’un personnage féminin jouable. Un nouveau visage féminin…
articles.txt:
Actualités Agenda Dossiers Expositions Scènes Musique Écrans Tendances Livres Podcasts Auteurs et Autrices Partenaires Qui sommes-nous? Contact Actualités Écrans Jeux vidéos GTA 6 : le personnage de Lucia peut-il changer la représentation des femmes dans le jeu vidéo ? par Rafaela Velasco 25.11.2026 Les fans de GTA ont enfin pu découvrir le sixième volet de la saga jeudi 19 novembre. Parmi les nouveautés : l’arrivée d’un personnage féminin jouable. Un nouveau visage féminin qui questionne les codes de la franchise, souvent critiquée pour ses portraits caricaturaux, sulfureux, voire misogynes.
Après plus de treize ans d’attente et plusieurs reports de date, le supplice prend fin pour les fans. Le 19 novembre, les adeptes de GTA ont enfin pu découvrir l’univers du 6ème volet de la saga . Dévoilée en décembre 2023, la bande-annonce de GTA 6 révélait les nouveaux personnages jouables de la version 2026 du jeu, dont une femme. Une première en trente ans de franchise. Dans les rues de Vice City, Jason Duval et Lucia Caminos, Bonnie and Clyde de ce Miami alternatif, sont pris dans une conspiration criminelle. Voitures, armes, courses-poursuites ; la saga GTA garde les codes de l’univers gangster inspiré du cinéma américain.
Le dernier opus, sorti en 2013, a fait de la franchise le deuxième jeu vidéo le plus vendu au monde, avec 235 millions d’exemplaires vendus. Une longévité qui lui a permis d’atteindre le statut de phénomène culturel. Mais le jeu est aussi décrié pour sa représentation des femmes et des minorités. Un parti pris assumé pendant plusieurs années par le studio Rockstar.
À quoi s’attendre quant à la représentation de ce personnage ? Jeune femme latino-américaine, Lucia incarne un certain renouveau dans l’univers du jeu, qui participe à traduire une réalité sociologique de Miami. Dans le trailer de lancement diffusé sur Netflix en août 2026, qui livre un meilleur aperçu de l’univers du jeu, on comprend qu’il sera possible de jouer les deux personnages. Fini le personnage accessoire, Lucia et Jason forment un couple de gangsters. Pour une fois, le jeu donne à son avatar féminin une histoire complexe et un caractère bien trempé.
Il faut dire que les précédents volets ont souvent réservé aux personnages féminins une place peu valorisante. Évoluant dans cet univers du gangstérisme, elles sont souvent reléguées à des rôles vulgairement dépeints, d’antagonistes traîtresses ou de travailleuses du sexe. Le gameplay permettait également au joueur d’adopter des comportements dégradants, voire violents envers ces personnages.
En 2022, l’association Women in Game proposait un état des lieux de la place des femmes dans l’écosystème du jeu vidéo. La même année, le CSA publiait un rapport dans lequel 9 % des femmes trouvaient que les personnages féminins dans les jeux vidéo n’étaient pas à l’image de la société. Pourtant, en 2022, en France, on comptait 18,8 millions de joueuses.
Même lorsqu’ils sont présents, les personnages féminins sont ancrés dans des stéréotypes de genre importants. Quant au visuel, ils sont encore souvent hypersexualisés. D’après le Geena Davis Institute en 2023, les personnages féminins ont dix fois plus de chances d’être montrés dans des vêtements sexy, voire d’apparaître nus à l’écran, que les personnages masculins.
Un constat confirmé dans un rapport du Sénat publié en juillet 2026, sur la persistance des biais sexistes dans l’industrie et ses imaginaires malgré une féminisation massive des publics.
Au cinéma, le test Bechdel évalue la représentation des femmes dans les productions cinématographiques. Avec son équipe de la chaire Diversité et Inclusion de l’EDHEC, Guergana Guintcheva, professeure de marketing culturel, a développé le Gender Parity Test. Son but : analyser le niveau de parité de genre des scripts de jeux vidéo. « Le jeu vidéo n’est pas un loisir passif, contrairement au cinéma. Les joueur.euses sont amenés à incarner un personnage, réaliser des actions. Son contenu narratif a donc une influence importante. »
Pour passer le test, le jeu doit répondre à quatre critères : est-ce qu’il inclut un nombre égal de personnages féminins et masculins ? Est-ce que ces personnages sont nommés en nombre égal ? Est-ce qu’ils sont jouables à un nombre égal ?
Dans la plupart des jeux vidéo, « beaucoup de personnages féminins sont uniquement en représentation, pas en action ».

GTA 6 : les meilleures voitures et où les trouver
articles.chapeau: Quelle est la meilleure voiture de GTA 6 ? Tout dépend de ce que vous cherchez : la vitesse, une conduite tout-terrain, une voiture à garder ou à revendre. Voici comment choisir, et où mettre la main sur votre prochain bolide.
articles.txt:
Depuis la Banshee de GTA III jusqu'à l' Infernus de Vice City , chaque épisode de la saga a ses voitures cultes, et les joueurs de Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) n'ont pas tardé à chercher les leurs. Supercars inspirées des grandes marques italiennes, muscle cars rétro, pick-up surélevés ou buggys tout-terrain : Leonida offre un choix immense.
Mais dans ce nouvel épisode, Rockstar Games a changé les règles du jeu : on ne s'offre plus une voiture comme on le faisait chez le concessionnaire de GTA V , et toutes ne se gardent pas aussi facilement. Vitesse, conduite, disponibilité, prix : voici comment choisir la voiture qui vous convient, et où la trouver.
Non, et c'est la première surprise pour les habitués de GTA V . Pas de concessionnaire ni de site internet pour commander une voiture : dans GTA 6 , on vole d'abord, puis on fait immatriculer le véhicule pour le garder. Une voiture volée et non immatriculée ne vous appartient pas, et elle peut disparaître.
Au début de l'aventure, Jason n'a que sa propre voiture, un pick-up Vapid Ganado de 1970. La possibilité de garder d'autres véhicules arrive au chapitre 2.
Tout passe par Moses, le receleur de Port Gellhorn, que vous rencontrez pendant la mission principale "Moses", au chapitre 2. La marche à suivre :
Repérez une voiture qui vous plaît et scannez-la avec l' application WAiNK de votre téléphone : elle affiche son système de sécurité, sa valeur et le prix de l'immatriculation. Au chapitre 2, choisissez une voiture sans traceur GPS, la seule que Moses accepte. Volez-la (le Slim Jim que vous donne Moses permet d'ouvrir les portières sans déclencher l'alarme), puis conduisez-la jusqu'à son garage. Choisissez de repeindre la voiture, puis sélectionnez Immatriculer au lieu de Vendre . Bonne nouvelle, la première immatriculation est gratuite : réservez-la à une voiture que vous comptez vraiment garder.
Ensuite, le prix de l'immatriculation augmente avec la valeur du véhicule, et peut dépasser 20 000 $ pour une sportive haut de gamme. À partir du chapitre 3, les Pay 'n' Spray prennent le relais et acceptent aussi les voitures équipées d'un traceur standard. Les voitures les plus prestigieuses, elles, ne peuvent pas être immatriculées en début de partie. Une fois votre voiture immatriculée, l'application Scooter Bros permet de vous la faire livrer n'importe où, contre une petite somme.
Chaque voiture immatriculée occupe une place de garage. Quand toutes vos places sont prises, il faut vendre un véhicule ou acheter un nouveau garage. Deux garages sont offerts par l'histoire : celui de la gare de Port Gellhorn , donné par Moses, et le Paradise Garage , au nord-est de Watson Bay , offert par Wyman aux possesseurs de l'édition Ultimate. Les autres s'achètent avec l'application immobilière de votre téléphone ou directement sur place :
Personne ne peut encore le dire avec certitude. Rockstar Games n'a publié aucune vitesse de pointe, et les classements qui circulent reprennent pour la plupart les chiffres de GTA V , qui ne valent pas forcément pour ce nouvel épisode. Méfiez-vous aussi des jauges du jeu, arrondies et peu fiables pour comparer deux bolides. Nous mettrons cet article à jour dès que des mesures sérieuses seront disponibles.
En attendant, les supercars les plus attendues sont bien présentes à Leonida, comme la Pegassi Tempesta , la Grotti Furia , la Truffade Thrax ou la Progen Emerus . Pour mettre la main sur les deux dernières sans chercher, il existe une solution : les codes de triche. La Thrax se débloque en terminant tous les défis de shopping, l'Emerus en terminant tous les défis de véhicules, et la Bravado Banshee , légende de la saga, en terminant tous les défis de combat. Ces codes ne s'utilisent qu'après la fin de l'histoire.
GTA 6 : la liste complète des codes de triche sur PS5 et Xbox Series Les codes de triche sont de retour dans GTA 6, mais impossible de les taper dès le début de la partie. Comment les débloquer sur PS5 et Xbox Series ? On fait le point. [Lire la suite]
Un conseil pour la conduite : gardez votre voiture immatriculée pour les trajets du quotidien et utilisez des véhicules volés pour les coups risqués. Une voiture personnelle envoyée à la fourrière coûte cher à récupérer.
Vendre des voitures est l'une des meilleures sources de revenus du jeu, mais le prix dépend de votre avancée :
Dans tous les cas, évitez les rayures et ne cassez pas les vitres pour entrer : le moindre dégât fait baisser le prix.

GTA 6 confirms what happened to Michael and Jimmy after GTA 5 in nostalgic easter egg
articles.chapeau: This may just be GTA 6's greatest hidden find so far 🙏
articles.txt:
Michael and Jimmy De Santa feature in the latest GTA 6 easter egg that's got us feeling all nostalgic.
Grand Theft Auto VI is packed to the rafters with easter eggs and secrets - and while it feels as if players have already discovered hundreds of examples, we’ll probably still be finding more five years from now.
You can be taken to Hell to fight Satan , dropped into a battle royale that’s equal parts The Hunger Games and Saw, or stumble across Mount Chiliad 2.0 . There’s no shortage of surprises in Leonida.
This latest find, however, is a tad more wholesome than some of those examples we’ve listed above, because GTA VI also confirms what happened to Michael and Jimmy following the events of Grand Theft Auto V .
GTA V can end a number of different ways, but Michael’s canon ending sees him leave behind his life of crime in pursuit of a career in the Vinewood film industry as a producer.
As for Jimmy, well, his canon ending also sees him survive and eventually move out of his parents house, much to Michael’s relief, we’re sure.
Jimmy quite prominently features within GTA VI - more on that later - but it’s a team-up between the duo that’s really made us nostalgic.
As shared by DiscussingFilm and found by X (formerly Twitter) user CaptainGlack, Michael and Jimmy went into production together on a film following the events of GTA V .
Across Vice City in GTA VI , you should be able to find film posters for ‘Righteous Slaughter Overkill’.
CaptainGlack was able to zoom in to see that the film credits both Michael De Santa and Jimmy De Santa, although it’s not clear whether they’re producers, directors, or something else.
Even still, it’s nice to see proof that Michael achieved his dream and even turned it into a family business.
If ‘Righteous Slaughter Overkill’ is ringing a bell, that’s because it appears across the Grand Theft Auto franchise a couple of times.
It’s actually GTA’s spoof version of Call of Duty. You can find characters wearing ‘Slaughter Hood Ops’ t-shirts in GTA VI, while in GTA V , Michael can watch Jimmy play ‘Righteous Slaughter 7’.
It’s pretty funny to think then that Jimmy showed his now-producer dad his favourite video game and got it turned into a major Hollywood - or Vinewood - blockbuster.
READ MORE: GTA 6 Criminal Profile explained: morality levels and avoiding Irredeemable status
It’s at this point that we’ll offer a spoiler warning in case you want to discover GTA VI ’s secrets and cameos at your own pace. You’ve been warned.
Jimmy actually shows up in GTA VI as a “crypto influencer” and self-declared “nepo baby”.
You’ll find him at the Jack of Hearts club in Vice City with Danny Temberelli returning to voice the character.
It’s a very brief interaction but it’s still a blast to run into this returning familiar face.

articles.chapeau: Take-Two Interactive is taking action against unofficial projects, with one of the biggest efforts to bring GTA 6 to PC already shut down.

Progress of unofficial PC ports for GTA 6 It has just been over a week since GTA 6 launched on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S, and modders have already made some noticeable progress in getting the game to run on PC. However, Rockstar Games and its parent company, Take-Two Interactive, are now taking action against these unofficial projects, with one of the biggest efforts to bring GTA 6 to PC already shut down.
🔥 More offers: see our Black Friday GTA 6 deals 2026 guide, updated daily, or browse all Black Friday deals .
For those unaware, notorious GTA 6 leaker Cyberleek released an alleged 209GB Xbox build of the game shortly after its launch. While the build contained a large collection of game files, it was initially missing the main executable. However, Cyberleek released the missing file on Monday, allowing modders to make further progress with their unofficial PC ports .
One of the most popular projects that emerged following the leak was Leonida, led by a developer known as NotRexed. The project attracted a lot of attention from the community and was aimed at getting the Xbox version of GTA 6 to run natively on PC. However, its GitHub repository suddenly became inaccessible recently, and we now have confirmation that Take-Two was behind its removal.
GitHub has published a DMCA takedown notice submitted by Take-Two’s intellectual property enforcement team. The company requested the removal of Leonida’s main repository along with thousands of copies of its code. According to GitHub, the takedown affected an entire network of 3,007 repositories.
Interestingly, the developers behind Leonida did not distribute the leaked GTA 6 files themselves. Instead, the project required users to provide their own game files. However, Take-Two argued that this approach was intentionally misleading, pointing to the timing of the project’s creation and its reliance on the unauthorized Xbox build circulating online.
Aside from the GitHub repository, Leonida’s Discord server was also taken down. Interestingly, NotRexed previously announced that he is stepping away from the project altogether. While Rockstar’s intervention contributed to his decision, he explained that managing the community alongside his personal commitments had also become increasingly difficult. However, he has now asked to “ignore” his other posts as “something’s coming soon.”
That said, Leonida isn’t the only project working on an unofficial GTA 6 PC port. Other modders have reportedly managed to get the game’s opening scenes running on PC, although they are still dealing with graphical issues and poor frame rates. There’s still a significant amount of work left before these unofficial ports can offer a proper gameplay experience.

GTA 6 tourne-t-il mieux sur PS5 ou Xbox Series X ? On connait enfin la réponse

Les experts de Digital Foundry révèlent en effet que la console de Microsoft offre une meilleure fluidité et souffre nettement moins de chutes de framerate.
articles.txt:
Malgré l’accord marketing signé par Sony autour de GTA 6, le blockbuster de Take-Two tourne mieux sur Xbox Series X que sur la PS5 classique. Les experts de Digital Foundry révèlent en effet que la console de Microsoft offre une meilleure fluidité et souffre nettement moins de chutes de framerate.
Sorti en brisant tous les records, GTA 6 est déjà le plus gros lancement de l’histoire du divertissement. Grâce à son accord marketing avec Take-Two, Sony et sa PS5 sont les autres grands gagnants de ce lancement historique. Mais malgré son slogan « Plays best on PS5 », les tests techniques indépendants de Digital Foundry , spécialistes de l’analyse technique, viennent raconter une tout autre histoire.
Avant d’aller plus loin, rappelons un autre fait : la version PS5 Pro est celle qui offre les meilleurs graphismes et la plus grande stabilité, et la version Xbox Series S est la moins impressionnante techniquement, même si le jeu reste parfaitement jouable sur cette console.
Ceci étant dit, Digital Foundry a étudié le comportement de GTA 6 sur les deux consoles les plus populaires de chaque constructeur : la PS5 et la Xbox Series X. Et cette dernière prend l’avantage techniquement parlant sur sa rivale nippone. En effet, la version PS5 subit des chutes de fréquence d’images (framerate) nettement plus fréquentes et marquées durant les séquences d’action intenses. Sur la machine de Microsoft, la puissance matérielle légèrement supérieure de la console permet de maintenir un affichage plus stable quand le nombre d’éléments à calculer à l’image devient très important.
À lire : GTA 6 démarre déjà sur PC quelques jours après sa sortie
Ajoutons à cela la prise en charge native du VRR (rafraîchissement variable) et du 120 Hz sur Xbox Series X , un atout technique qui permet d’atténuer les ralentissements sur les téléviseurs compatibles. Dans les faits, les joueurs ne vont pas s’amuser à compter les pixels et les images par seconde en plein jeu, mais Digital Foundry note que dans certaines situations de jeu, la Xbox Series X s’en sort mieux que la PS5 standard.
Rappelons que c’est la présence de la technologie d’upscaling FSR 4.1 d’AMD qui a permis à GTA 6 de tourner sur Xbox Series S. La Xbox Series X ne l’utilise pas pour le jeu de RockStar, ce qui veut dire qu’il existe encore une marge de progression pour la console haut de gamme de Microsoft.
À lire : J’ai joué à GTA 6 sur ma vieille Xbox One grâce au cloud : voilà à quoi ça ressemble
Sur cette génération de consoles, PlayStation a clairement dominé Xbox en matière de ventes. Le partenariat entre la marque japonaise et Take-Two pour le lancement de GTA 6 vient enfoncer le clou avec un nombre de précommande du jeu largement supérieur sur la console de Sony. Ajoutez à cela les contraintes d’approvisionnement matériel importantes que rencontrent les consoles, la PS5 est en rupture de stock un peu partout , et on comprend mieux pourquoi la nouvelle dirigeante de la marque Xbox, Asha Sharma, a déjà le regard tourné vers la prochaine génération de consoles.

articles.chapeau: Vous comptiez sur le Black Friday pour vous offrir une PlayStation 5 ? Bonne chance car GTA 6 a provoqué une rupture de stock mondiale !!!
articles.txt:
Vous comptiez profiter du Black Friday pour enfin vous offrir une PS5 et suivre les aventures de Lucia et Jason ? Mieux vaut vous armer de patience, voire d’une bonne dose de chance ! Moins d’une semaine après le lancement de Grand Theft Auto VI, le jeudi 19 novembre, la console de Sony affiche sold out chez une bonne partie des enseignes. Outre-Atlantique, la boutique officielle PlayStation Direct, Best Buy et Amazon étaient tous en rupture dans la nuit du 24 au 25 novembre, et la situation n’est guère plus réjouissante de notre côté de l’océan.
En France aussi, les rayons se sont vidés à vitesse grand V. La Fnac, Darty, Cultura, Micromania ou encore la plupart des grandes surfaces n’ont plus rien à proposer, tandis que le site de Sony se contente d’indiquer que l’article ne peut pas être commandé. Certes, quelques lots refont parfois surface, mais ils s’envolent souvent en quelques minutes, si bien qu’il faut guetter les alertes de réassort jour et nuit. Quant à la PS5 Pro, déjà rare depuis plusieurs mois, elle est presque devenue une légende urbaine depuis la sortie du titre de Rockstar.
Il faut dire que le jeu lui-même explique en grande partie cette ruée. Puisque GTA 6 tourne uniquement sur PS5 et sur les Xbox Series, sans version PS4 ni PC pour l’instant, tous les retardataires qui n’avaient pas encore changé de console se sont précipités au même moment. D’ailleurs, Sony s’en est félicité le 23 novembre en dressant un premier bilan. D’après ses données internes, plus de 39 millions de personnes ont démarré l’aventure sur PS5 entre le 19 et le 22 novembre, un record absolu pour un lancement chez PlayStation. Mieux encore, le constructeur japonais n’avait jamais vu autant de machines branchées pour la première fois sur une même journée depuis 2020, hors période des fêtes, et sept nouvelles consoles sur dix ont démarré leur carrière avec GTA 6. Autant dire que beaucoup de PS5 ont été achetées uniquement pour arpenter l’État de Leonida !
Au final, inutile d’espérer une remise sur la console de Sony cette semaine, puisque l’enjeu sera surtout d’en voir une en rayon. Et vous, avez-vous pu acheter votre PS5 avant la pénurie, ou comptez-vous attendre le prochain réassort pour plonger dans GTA 6 ?

articles.chapeau: GTA 6 crash reports are piling up on PS5, with two streamers
articles.txt:
GTA 6 has prompted reports of PS5 crashes, shutdowns and hardware failures, including two streamers whose consoles died or smoked during play. Testing measured 274.2W draw, within the console's power budget. No causal link is proven, though demand may expose cooling problems in older models.

Rockstar Games' Grand Theft Auto 6 launched on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S on November 19, and less than a week later, reports of PS5 crashes, sudden shutdowns, and even dead consoles are piling up, with two Twitch streamers losing their consoles in the middle of a session.
The most dramatic case comes from Twitch streamer shivjam, who posted that GTA 6 had " fried my PS5. The GPU is done and the console is gone. "
In the clip, the game freezes as green artifacts streak across the screen, a symptom usually associated with failing graphics hardware, and Notebookcheck reports the console then refused to boot despite troubleshooting. shivjam later shared photos of the console's fans to push back on claims that dust was to blame.
Before that, streamer JoJoJosiah said his PS5 started smoking while GTA 6 was paused on stream, and that he now needs a replacement.
So, is GTA 6 actually killing PS5 consoles? There's no evidence of that yet. Console repair technician modyfikatorcasper measured his PS5 pulling 274.2W at the wall in a max-load GTA 6 test, calling the game " the toughest real-world PS5 stress test I've seen. "
A typical game peaks at 180 to 220W, while Sony designed the PS5 to draw up to 340 to 350W, which puts GTA 6 at the high end but still inside the console's power budget. The technician suspects the heavy load is exposing weak cooling on older base PS5 models. Notably, far more players are reporting crashes than dead hardware, with error code CE-108255-1 the most common, and reports indicate that Rockstar's first patch didn't fix it.

articles.t: 'GTA 6' on PC: What we know about the PC release
articles.chapeau: 'Grand Theft Auto VI' is here for console gamers, but remains one of the most-anticipated video games of all time on PC.
articles.txt:
Grand Theft Auto VI is available on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S consoles at launch (it will also be available on Xbox Cloud Gaming , with limits).
GTA 6 has no confirmed PC release date. Given Rockstar's history with PC ports, we originally thought gamers were in for a long wait.
An October 2026 report from gaming business media site Gamesbeat reveals a potential PC launch in early 2027, which is sooner than we expected.
Grand Theft Auto VI arrived on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S on Nov. 19, 2026, but PC players will have to wait a while longer. Rockstar has confirmed that the game will not be available for PC gamers at launch, and no PC version has been officially announced yet.
Despite that, we recently got some good news: GamesBeat reports that GTA 6 will get a PC release sometime in Q1 of 2027. GamesBeat has a good track record with unannounced news like this. According to their reporting, the GTA 6 PC release window was confirmed by industry sources familiar with Rockstar's plans. They spoke with the outlet under the condition of anonymity.
Rockstar and Take-Two haven't given an official reason for skipping PC at launch, but a few factors are typically cited when publishers stagger releases this way.
Console hardware is standardized, which tends to make optimization more straightforward than building for the huge range of PC configurations. Some industry data has also indicated that consoles generate higher per-unit revenue, giving publishers an incentive to front-load console sales.
A more cynical take is that Take-Two could just be double-dipping, hoping fans who can't wait for the PC launch will buy the console first, then buy the PC version later. A PC Gamer poll found that 39 percent of respondents said they're fine waiting for a port rather than needing it on day one, suggesting a meaningful share of the PC audience isn't treating the delay as a dealbreaker.
However, there could be another, less financially motivated reason for all of this.
Speaking to YouTuber KiwiTalkz , former Rockstar producer John Ricchio explained that building for consoles first and scaling up to PC is technically easier than the reverse, since consoles have fixed, predictable hardware. According to IGN , Ricchio said it's simpler to start with tighter constraints and add polish later than to build a PC-first game and then try to trim it down to fit console limitations.
Without an official release date, gamers have had to speculate on the most likely launch window for a GTA 6 PC version.
If you look at several past Rockstar games, you can see that there's typically a significant amount of time between the console launch and the PC port.
Grand Theft Auto 4 was released in April 2008 and didn't reach PC's until December. Grand Theft Auto V was released in Sept. 2013, and its PC counterpart was released 19 months later in April 2015. Red Dead Redemption 2 arrived on PC roughly a year after its console release.
The one exception was Grand Theft Auto: The Trilogy – The Definitive Edition , which launched simultaneously across platforms in 2021. Based on that track record, a GTA 6 PC port, if it follows the usual pattern, could be a year or more away.
A report from The Verge claimed that Xbox would have exclusive rights to stream GTA 6 via its cloud gaming service at launch, a claim that was recently confirmed. The report noted that PC gamers would be able to play GTA 6 on day one , despite Rockstar's lack of news about a potential release window for a PC port. Unfortunately, Xbox Gaming's Chief Strategy Officer, Matthew Ball, shot down this report. Ball wrote on his personal X account that The Verge's coverage led to some "misreporting."
Again, the game will be available to play on Xbox consoles via Xbox Cloud Gaming, but that service faces strict monthly limits, which will make it difficult to play through the game in a timely fashion.
Fortunately, a GamesBeat report suggests gamers may not have to wait a full year for a PC release, though it remains unconfirmed.

articles.txt:
Depuis quelques jours, les joueurs sur PS5 et sur Xbox Series S ou X peuvent jouer à GTA 6. En revanche, ceux qui jouent sur PC doivent encore patienter, puisque le jeu n’est pas encore disponible sur cette plateforme et Rockstar Games n’a pas encore évoqué de date. Néanmoins, celui-ci aurait tout intérêt à accélérer le développement de la version PC de GTA 6 puisque sur internet, de nombreux projets pour créer un portage non officiel du jeu vidéo ont déjà été lancés. Selon les explications de PC Mag, tout a commencé par une fuite.
Vendredi, le hacker Cyberleek aurait posté une fuite de la version Xbox de GTA 6 , complétée par un exécutable clé partagé lundi. Ces fichiers ne permettent pas de jouer à GTA 6 sur PC (et ce serait du piratage), mais, comme la plateforme Xbox est proche du PC, ils pourraient servir de base pour créer un GTA 6 pour PC non officiel. Et, justement, le but de hacker était de passer le flambeau aux communautés open source.
Par ailleurs, certaines “communautés” commenceraient déjà à obtenir des résultats, en s’aidant de l’IA afin de faire de l’ingénierie inversée et de recompiler GTA 6 pour PC. Sur les réseaux sociaux, des vidéos montreraient que certains développeurs ont déjà réussi à démarrer le jeu sur PC, même si c’est pour le moment injouable.
Bien entendu, Rockstar Games ne reste pas les bras croisés face à ces tentatives de créer une version non officielle de GTA 6 sur PC. En effet, si quelqu’un réussissait à développer une expérience de jeu acceptable, cela plomberait les ventes de GTA 6 et surtout de la future version pour PC officielle. Sur X, une personne qui aurait déjà énormément avancé sur son projet de recompilation aurait annoncé abandonner, en partie parce que son serveur Discord a été fermé. Et, d’après le site Torrentfreak , à quelques heures du lancement de GTA 6, des projets de portage du jeu vidéo pour l’iPhone, le Mac et Android avaient déjà été fermés par GitHub.
Comme évoqué plus haut, on ne sait pas quand Rockstar lancera GTA 6 sur PC. Mais, selon les rumeurs, il est possible que cette version pour PC arrive dès le premier trimestre 2027. En attendant, il est préférable de ne pas cliquer si vous tombez sur un lien sur internet qui vous promet une version de GTA 6 sur PC.
En effet, des hackers essaient déjà de profiter de la frustration des joueurs sur PC pour piéger ceux-ci. Par exemple, dans un précédent article, nous avons évoqué un faux guide sous format PDF qui pousse les internautes à télécharger un malware. Et, d’après une publication de NordVPN , des kits d’arnaque pour piéger les internautes sont aussi commercialisés sur le dark web.
That’s what our Threat Intelligence team found on the dark web: a crypto wallet drainer, a fake “GTA6 Keygen.exe” that steals accounts, a YouTube Shorts bot to spread it, and a hidden crypto miner.

articles.chapeau: Quelques heures après la dernière fuite de Cyberleek, des moddeurs font déjà booter GTA 6 sur PC, écran titre et menus à l’appui. Mais derrière ces exploits spectaculaires, que vaut vraiment ce fameux « GTA 6 jouable sur PC » qui affole les réseaux ?
articles.txt:
Quelques heures après la dernière fuite de Cyberleek, des moddeurs font déjà booter GTA 6 sur PC, écran titre et menus à l’appui. Mais derrière ces exploits spectaculaires, que vaut vraiment ce fameux « GTA 6 jouable sur PC » qui affole les réseaux ?
Quelques heures après la mise en ligne du fichier exécutable Xbox de GTA 6 par le hacker Cyberleek , des moddeurs sont déjà parvenus à lancer le jeu sur PC. Sur certaines configurations, le logo de Rockstar Games apparaît, l’écran titre se charge, puis la séquence de configuration initiale défile comme sur console avant de planter. Pour un titre officiellement limité à la PS5 et à la Xbox Series, la vitesse des progrès surprend même les habitués de la scène modding.
Tout est parti de la fuite d’une build Xbox Series d’environ 209 Go, publiée le 19 novembre, mais inutilisable sur PC sans son exécutable. D’après Notebookcheck, ce dernier a été ajouté quelques jours plus tard, déclenchant une véritable course contre la montre pour faire booter GTA 6 nativement sous Windows. Où en est vraiment ce portage non officiel, et faut-il déjà croire aux vidéos de « GTA 6 jouable sur PC » qui envahissent les réseaux ?
La clé, c’est que la version Xbox Series de GTA 6 repose sur une architecture processeur x86-64, la même famille que la majorité des PC de jeu. Les kits de développement Xbox utilisent des API proches de DirectX 12, ce qui réduit la distance technique à parcourir pour Windows. Plutôt que d’émuler entièrement la console, les moddeurs peuvent réécrire une partie des appels système et traduire les shaders pour qu’ils soient acceptés par un GPU PC.
Résultat : alors qu’au départ le jeu se contentait de lancer l’exécutable avant de crasher immédiatement, Notebookcheck rapporte qu’il passe désormais l’écran de boot et tout l’outil de configuration initiale. Certaines équipes affirment même atteindre la cinématique d’intro autour de 30 à 40 images par seconde, mais aucun monde ouvert jouable et stable n’a été montré de façon crédible.
Un moddeur mentionne déjà environ 770 Go occupés sur SSD après décompression du dump Xbox et recompilation de plus de 26 000 shaders, ce qui donne une idée du chantier. À ce stade, l’expérience se limite à faire démarrer l’exécutable Xbox, afficher les menus et observer où le jeu plante pour corriger les appels manquants. Aucun installateur simple ni lanceur Windows « prêt à cliquer » n’existe pour le grand public.
Parallèlement, d’autres bidouilles ont consisté à faire tourner GTA 6 via une PS5 en streaming local sur PC, puis à injecter le DLSS 5 de Nvidia . Le DLSS est une technique qui rend le jeu dans une résolution plus basse puis reconstruit une image plus nette, ce qui permet de débloquer le frame rate au‑delà de 30 fps et d’améliorer la fluidité. Mais là encore, on reste dans le domaine de la démonstration technique, pas d’un port PC natif et distribué.
Notebookcheck estime qu’au rythme actuel, une build PC non officielle pourrait apparaître sur des sites de piratage dans les jours à venir. Cela ne signifie pas pour autant une version stable : la plupart de ces « GTA 6 PC full version » ont toutes les chances d’être des malwares déguisés , capables de voler mots de passe, comptes de jeu ou cryptomonnaies. Juridiquement, télécharger et exécuter ces fichiers reste de toute façon illégal.
Officiellement, Rockstar Games et Take-Two Interactive n’ont annoncé aucun port PC de GTA 6 . La seule façon légale d’y jouer sur ordinateur reste le Remote Play ou le cloud depuis sa propre console. Dans le même temps, l’auteur de la fuite se justifie : selon Notebookcheck, Cyberleek affirme « se battre contre les fonctionnalités verrouillées derrière des paywalls et les 20 dollars facturés en plus pour l’Ultimate Edition », tout en utilisant un memecoin $CYBERLEEK pour financer son projet, sans le rendre obligatoire pour accéder aux fichiers. Rockstar chercherait activement à l’identifier par des moyens juridiques, pour l’instant sans succès.
Au final, oui, GTA 6 boote déjà sur certains PC de moddeurs, ce qui est un signal fort sur la proximité technique entre Xbox Series et Windows. Mais non, il n’existe toujours pas de « GTA 6 jouable sur PC » accessible, fiable et sûr pour le joueur lambda. Pour l’instant, le feuilleton profite surtout aux passionnés de reverse engineering et aux cybercriminels à l’affût des plus impatients.

Rockstar's response to the first serious attempt at a GTA 6 PC port appears to have landed just as hard as its warning against AI-assisted PC clones and reverse engineering.
Project Leonida, the biggest fan recompilation effort, has been scrapped after its Discord server and GitHub repository vanished, just hours after it showed the game getting further than anyone expected.
As we covered, notorious leaker Cyberleek released a near-complete Xbox build of the game , then followed up on November 23 with the missing executable . Within hours, Leonida's Discord reported that "the game almost boots," with a black screen and cut-off audio. Later footage appeared to show the full opening sequence and first-time setup running on PC.
By then, the project had been working with help from Claude AI to recompile the leaked Xbox build for Windows. A few hours later, it was gone. Lead developer NotRexed announced he was quitting. "I quit, guys. I'm sorry. I really want to make cool stuff, but every single time shit happens that I can't control, so I'm stepping away."
In a follow-up, he blamed Rockstar for the server takedown, but said it was only part of the reason. "Like I've said before, I'm a 15 year-old kid. Managing school and sports is hard enough without having middle-aged men yell and complain to you on Discord. Goodbye."
The Discord server had almost 180,000 members when it went offline, and NotRexed says he has been banned from Discord for two years. His original GitHub repository is also gone, though clones made by others appear to remain online.
Rockstar hasn't commented publicly, so its involvement rests on the developer's own account. Still, it would fit a pattern. Take-Two recently shut down the unofficial GTA V Android and Switch ports from Paralympics Productions with a cease-and-desist. There are also Reddit reports that Rockstar is going after other GTA 6 Discord servers, including one said to have around six million members, though that is unconfirmed.

articles.chapeau: Just wait for the official PC version of the game to come out.
articles.txt:
Don't try to port Grand Theft Auto VI to PC yourself — or you'll potentially find yourself in big legal trouble.
GTA 6 may finally be out on Xbox and PlayStation 5, but that doesn't help out the PC gaming faithful, who still have much longer to wait for their version of the game.
As a result, some impatient gamers have recently attempted to create PC ports of the game themselves. Notorious GTA 6 leaker, Cyberleek, also recently released an executable .exe file of the Xbox build of the game, which helped those efforts. Even without Cyberleek, these efforts were probably inevitable, as new AI tools have led to a surge in PS5 jailbreaks and unauthorized ports of classic video games.
However, Rockstar Games' parent company, Take-Two Interactive, clearly does not approve of these unofficial attempts to bring GTA 6 to PC ahead of schedule. On Monday, the company had the biggest GTA 6 PC port project, known as Leonida, taken down. So far, GTA 6 has generated billions of dollars, and the PC version could bring in billions more. And when it comes to protecting their IP, Take-Two and Rockstar aren't messing around.
GitHub, where the project was hosted, posted a Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA) notice it received from Take-Two.
"We are the IP Enforcement Team for Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc., parent company of Rockstar Games," the notice reads. "We are writing to submit a takedown request regarding ItsNotRexed's GitHub repository and the 2900+ forks attached to it that infringes upon Take-Two's copyrighted works and facilitates copyright infringement of Rockstar Games title, Grand Theft Auto VI."

"On November 20, 2026, stolen game files from an Xbox Series build of Grand Theft Auto VI were publicly distributed," the takedown notice reads. "The following day, this Leonida repository opened with the purpose of running the Xbox Series version of GTA VI on PC. Its README requires Xbox Series game files as input."
According to Take-Two, Leonida attempts to get around the IP issues by instructing project contributors to "bring your own files."
"This is intentionally misleading," Take-Two explains, pointing out that the files in question are the unauthorized GTA 6 files leaked by Cyberleek.
As our colleagues at PCMag point out , this is just one of many unauthorized projects attempting to bring GTA 6 to PC before the official version comes out. (Disclosure: Mashable and PCMag are both owned by the same parent company, Ziff Davis.) Other projects have reportedly managed to get the game's opening scene running on PC. Another has an extremely degraded version of the game running on Mac.
According to the Leonida project admin , Take-Two also successfully had the Discord server for the GTA 6 porting project taken down as well, so it does seem like the company is going to ramp up its takedowns of any attempted GTA 6 ports.
GTA 6 for PC has no official release date. However, GameBeat recently reported that the PC version may be released in early 2027, well before most gamers expected.

articles.txt:
Cyberleek has released the missing executable for the leaked 209GB Grand Theft Auto 6 Xbox build ahead of schedule, giving modders and reverse-engineering groups another piece of the puzzle as they work toward getting the game running on PC. The release follows a cryptocurrency fundraising campaign tied to a $15 million meme coin market cap target, which was later reduced to $6 million.
The original Xbox files began circulating on November 19 , but the package lacked an essential .exe file, preventing anyone from attempting to launch the build. Cyberleek had initially promised to distribute the missing executable once tonce the November 23rd deadline passed,. However, the file started appearing on piracy websites just before the countdown expired .
Although its arrival is a significant development for people examining the leaked build, it does not mean GTA VI is suddenly playable on Windows. Cyberleek previously predicted that developers could produce a bootable PC version within a week, potentially through emulation or by adapting the game to run natively.
Neither approach is straightforward, as developers still face substantial technical challenges, including shader translation , memory management, and adapting the game's software environment to Windows. One such open-source compatibility layer project, VIctory , aims to translate GPU shaders and recreate console-specific features so GTA VI 's Xbox x86-64 code can run directly on Windows. Anyone struggling to keep track of the numerous projects can now follow their progress in one place on PortWatchVI .
Cyberleek also included a text document alongside the executable, reiterating the motivations behind the leak and the cryptocurrency campaign. According to the message, previous GTA 6 gameplay leaks deliberately avoided major story spoilers because the intention was not to ruin the experience for players. Instead, Cyberleek directed criticism toward Rockstar Games and its parent company, Take-Two Interactive, particularly over the delayed arrival of a dedicated PC version.
For now, the executable represents another development in the ongoing effort to examine the leaked Xbox build, rather than an immediate route to playing GTA 6 on PC. Whether the wider project delivers anything beyond the current leaks remains to be seen.

A Manifold Markets question asking whether Grand Theft Auto VI will be decompiled within a month of release is priced as close to a coin flip, around 50% implied probability of YES as of November 24, 2026, with roughly 140 holders and more than 500 trades logged. The catalyst is not a confirmed decompilation. It is the November 23 release of an executable for an alleged 209 GB Xbox Series X|S build, five days after Rockstar launched the game on consoles with no PC version. Within hours, community recompilation projects were loading the game world on Windows, and the largest of them deleted itself.

The question, “Will GTA 6 be decompiled within a month of release” , was created by Manifold user gallerdude and resolves on a 31-day window measured from the official global retail release. Rockstar shipped the game on November 19, 2026, which puts resolution around December 20.
The criteria are stricter than the title implies. Per the description, a YES requires a reverse-engineered source repository, written in a high-level language such as C or C++, published publicly online, that compiles and runs at least the introductory sequence or first playable mission. It must be reconstructed from retail binaries, and an official source code leak does not count.
That wording is load-bearing. What the modding scene has produced so far is not a decompilation in that sense, but a set of static-recompilation and compatibility layers, a different technical object with a different legal profile.
As of November 24, 2026, the decompilation market on Manifold sits at roughly 50% YES, having traded in the high 40s to low 50s since the executable dropped, across about 140 holders and more than 500 trades.
Two caveats come first. Manifold runs on mana, a play-money currency, so the incentive to price carefully is reputational rather than financial, and 140 holders is a thin pool in which a few confident traders can move the number by double digits.
A sister market is pricing the easier version of the same question higher. “Will GTA6 be recompiled on a PC build before November 30, 2026?”, created by Manifold user apol , sat at 63% as of November 24 across 47 holders. That one requires a functional native x86-64 Windows build that boots into an interactive in-engine environment, verified by a named outlet or shipped as a reproducible public repository. We tracked that market’s climb in our breakdown of the 63% recompile odds .
The 13-point gap between the two is the most informative number here. Traders are more confident that something will boot on Windows than that anyone will publish reconstructed C or C++ source. Those are not the same bar, and the cheaper one is closer to reality.
CyberLeek, the persona behind the long-running GTA VI leak campaign, resurfaced at launch with what they claimed was a near-complete Xbox build. Video Games Chronicle and PC Gamer both reported a roughly 200 GB package circulating by torrent, close to the game’s console install footprint, containing assets, RAGE engine files and shaders.
It shipped without its central executable, which made it inert. CyberLeek set a countdown and said the file would follow. XDA Developers reported the executable for build 1.0.2.1 going out on November 23 with the message “the exe is out. Always free.”
Neither Rockstar Games nor Take-Two Interactive has publicly authenticated the archive or the executable. Every claim about what the build contains traces back to CyberLeek or to developers who say the files work in their tooling.
The effort is spread across several named projects, tracked publicly by the community site PortWatch VI .

As we previously reported , developers managed to boot GTA 6 on PC within three hours of the executable's release. At the time, progress was limited to the game's initial settings and legal screens, with no actual playable areas.
Now, multiple Xbox-to-PC compatibility projects are making progress toward rendering the game's 3D environments, with portions of the development process reportedly being streamed live on Discord.
One of these projects, called VIctory , is an open-source compatibility layer designed to execute GTA 6's original Xbox x86-64 code directly on Windows while reimplementing console-specific functionality and translating GPU shaders.
3 VIctory is an open-source compatibility layer for running the Xbox Series X|S build of GTA 6 on Windows; the project reports reaching the first mission’s intro, but most of the scene still fails to render. (Image: Github) VIEW GALLERY - 3 IMAGES According to the project's November 23 development update, testing on a Windows 11 system equipped with an AMD Radeon RX 6700 XT has demonstrated 30 FPS in the menus, working save functionality, and intro video playback with audio. The project also loads into the game world in about 50 seconds, reaching the first mission's introductory sequence.
However, rendering remains severely limited, with most of the scene missing and individual frames taking between 0.5 and 1.8 seconds to render, equivalent to approximately 0.6 - 2 FPS. Entering the game world can also cause GPU hangs and display driver resets.
Interestingly, Reddit user u/bingusmakesbread has shared footage purportedly showing further progress, including partially functioning shaders, character models, and environmental rendering.
The user clarified that the footage originates from a separate private project that could eventually be integrated into one of the existing public projects or released independently.
The architectural similarities between Microsoft's Xbox Series consoles and modern Windows PCs help explain the rapid progress. Rather than emulating an entirely different CPU architecture, developers can focus on translating console-specific graphics functionality and implementing the necessary system services.
There is also a significant obstacle regarding game ownership and distribution. Even so, Xbox Series X|S owners running up-to-date firmware reportedly have no straightforward way to extract their own decrypted copy of GTA 6 for use with these projects.
There's a live tracker called Portwatch that monitors projects that recompile, emulate, or port the leaked Xbox Series build to PC. At the time of writing, VIctory sits at 67% completion; note this scale is not linear: 55% is reached at the main menu, 70% when in-game, 85% at 30 FPS, and 100% when stable. The last stretch will likely need much more development time, effort, and AI tokens.
3 Portwatch puts the leading unofficial GTA 6 PC project at 72% on its progress scale, past the in-game milestone but short of the 30 FPS mark. (Image: Portwatch) Story Q&A Powered by TweakBot

articles.t: Benchmark finds GTA 6 PS5 performance inferior to Xbox Series X, with more framerate drops
articles.chapeau: GTA 6 on the Xbox Series X has fewer performance drawbacks than on the base PS5. Digital Foundry discovered that framerates stay closer to the 30 fps target on the Microsoft system. VRR at 120Hz also helps the Series X maintain smoother graphics in congested Leonida scenes.
articles.txt:
A new benchmark shows how the GTA 6 Xbox Series X version outshines the base PS5 alternative . Digital Foundry compared performance on the rival consoles. While the differences aren’t enormous, the Rockstar title exhibited more infrequent framerate drops on Microsoft’s hardware.
Image quality is very similar on the Series X and the most affordable PlayStation . Both platforms support features like ray-traced global illumination and reflections. At 30 fps , the native 1440p resolution upscales to 4K, with temporal anti-aliasing (TAA) smoothing out jagged edges. Digital Foundry observed only minor variations in how effects like heat haze render.
The two consoles begin to diverge during fast-action gameplay , driving , or crowded Leonida environments . When Lucia races through a packed airport, framerates fall into the mid to upper 20s. Explosions worsen the stuttering, pushing readings closer to 20 fps. The GTA 6 PS5 version fares slightly worse in the most demanding scenes.
Framerates are more stable on GTA 6 Xbox benchmarks. Still, VRR at 120Hz produces the biggest disparity. On compatible displays, Microsoft’s system employs low framerate compensation (LFC) at below 48 fps. The base PlayStation doesn’t have that capability, making performance seem inconsistent.
The site calls the results “surprising,” but the Rockstar project is a unique case. Pushing hardware to its limits, the marginally superior Series X GPU benefits. Although the PS5 chip runs at a higher clock speed, it has 44% fewer compute units.
Amplifying demand for a PC port , no console achieves greater than 30 fps. Regardless, Digital Foundry confirmed GTA 6 on the PS5 Pro is the best existing option. Aided by PSSR 2 upscaling , the 4K output looks noticeably crisper. Meanwhile, ray-traced shadows make already realistic scenery more lifelike. Framerates are steadier, rarely dipping under its target.
For budget-conscious gamers, the Xbox Series S may introduce fewer performance compromises than expected. Unique to the console, FSR 4.1 boosts the native 720p resolution to a respectable 1080p. Even so, lower-quality shadows are apparent, along with audio drops that updates have not yet addressed.

articles.t: The Hacker Who Leaked GTA 6 in 2022 Has Been Sentenced: Judge Calls Him “A Very Talented Young Man” Before Handing Down His Punishment | LEVEL UP
articles.chapeau: Arion Kurtaj became notorious for breaching the security of major companies using nothing more than a phone and an Amazon Fire TV Stick when he was 17
articles.txt:
In 2022, Rockstar Games went into a panic when a major Grand Theft Auto VI leak appeared online. The most anticipated game in history became a hot topic on social media and forums after its first images and details were revealed.
Some time later, the person responsible was caught: Arion Kurtaj. His story became notorious because, at just 17 years old, he managed to compromise the security systems of Rockstar, Revolut, Uber, and other companies using nothing more than a smartphone and an Amazon Fire TV Stick.
His hacking spree came to an end with his arrest, confinement in a psychiatric facility, and the sentence he received after pleading guilty.
The moment of truth arrived for Arion Kurtaj, now 21, before the judge overseeing his case at Woolwich Crown Court. It’s worth remembering that, days before the game’s release, the young man pleaded guilty in an attempt to avoid prison.
Although the possibility of spending years behind bars was real, a BBC report revealed that the authorities showed leniency toward the young hacker, who was part of the Lapsus$ group.
The judge determined that the time Arion Kurtaj had spent in pretrial detention and subsequently in a psychiatric institution had been sufficient in terms of confinement and restrictions on his social life.
As a result, he was sentenced to conditional release under a Serious Crime Prevention Order that will remain in effect for 5 years. During this period, the young hacker will not be allowed to engage in online activities or use platforms such as Telegram and Discord.
Arion Kurtaj, the hacker who brought Rockstar Games to its knees in 2022.
The proceedings established that Arion Kurtaj had committed a crime, which is why he was held in custody while awaiting the outcome of his case and the corresponding sentence.
However, the unusual circumstances surrounding his actions surprised the authorities. The young man managed to cause major problems for important companies using everyday devices such as a smartphone and an Amazon Fire Stick from a hotel.
That’s why the judge who sentenced him praised his abilities, while also expressing hope that he would use his talent for good and never reoffend:
“You are a very talented young man. Don’t let this happen again.”
Four years ago, Rockstar Games said it was disappointed by the leak, particularly because it revealed an important detail about GTA 6: the game would feature a female protagonist, whom we now know to be Lucia Caminos.

articles.t: CyberLeek Leaks GTA 6’s Executable File, and Modders Are Already Working on a Playable PC Version | LEVEL UP
articles.chapeau: The hacker says its actions are a protest against major companies such as Rockstar Games and Take-Two Interactive
articles.txt:
CyberLeek resurfaced this week to fulfill its promise and leak the executable file for Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6), taken from an Xbox version of the game. This has allowed the modding community to start working on an unofficial PC port.
Of course, Rockstar Games hasn’t been sitting idly by. The company obviously wants to stop an illegal version of GTA 6 from making its way to computers and possibly consoles. In fact, it has already made its first move to shut down the project and prevent piracy from affecting its popular title, which, according to estimates, has already sold more than 44 million copies.
Its efforts have paid off, as the company recently dealt a major blow to the development of the GTA 6 PC port. As a result, one of its creators threw in the towel and decided to abandon the project.
CyberLeek recently made the executable file for GTA 6 public, corresponding to version 1.0.2.1 for Xbox Series X|S. This file opens the door to the development of illegal ports of the game, as a previous build had already been leaked and used by modders to launch a project that has put Rockstar Games on edge.
The project now facing trouble is Project Leonida, the name of the unofficial GTA 6 PC port. Rockstar has taken action to prevent its development from being completed. This comes after those behind the project showed significant progress, including footage of the game running and its opening sequence playing, albeit with some issues.
However, the project’s future is now uncertain, as the developer managed to halt its progress with a single move. Specifically, Rockstar succeeded in shutting down Project Leonida’s Discord server, prompting the project’s lead developer to walk away.
Modder NotRexed confirmed on social media that Project Leonida’s Discord server was now a thing of the past because Rockstar had stepped in. In response, he decided to abandon development of the unofficial GTA 6 PC port.
“I’m done, guys. I’m sorry. I really want to create cool things, but things I can’t control always get in the way, so I’m stepping down. Thank you to everyone, especially those on Discord, who gave me this opportunity,” NotRexed said.
He later explained that he was tired of dealing with the community’s demands and that the pressures of everyday life were preventing him from continuing development. NotRexed deleted his GitHub repositories, so this appears to be the definitive end of Project Leonida, although someone else could still take over development.
“Rockstar shutting down my server was only part of the problem. As I’ve said before, I’m a 15-year-old kid. It’s already hard enough balancing school and sports without having to put up with middle-aged men yelling at you and complaining on Discord. Goodbye,” NotRexed concluded.
The unofficial GTA 6 PC port has halted development following Rockstar Games’ actions.
Rockstar has a lot of work ahead if it wants to prevent an unofficial port of its open-world game from being released and potentially pirated on consoles. The thing is, Project Leonida isn’t the only initiative attempting to bring GTA 6 to other platforms by taking advantage of CyberLeek’s leaks.
There are currently at least a dozen similar projects seeking to run GTA 6 on PC before an official port arrives. In theory, Rockstar’s version would be released sometime in 2027, but no exact release date has been confirmed so far.
It’s highly likely that Rockstar and Take-Two Interactive’s legal teams will also attempt to shut down these projects. At Level Up, we want to emphasize that we do NOT support these kinds of initiatives. Meanwhile, a mysterious GTA 6 page has appeared on Steam, although there are serious suspicions that it could be a scam.

articles.t: GTA 6 EXE Leak: 57 MB File, 0 Playable PC Builds
articles.chapeau: CyberLeek released a 57 MB GTA 6 executable for Xbox build 1.0.2.1. It does not run the game, and Project Leonida has no playable PC build.
articles.txt:
Image: Rockstar Games CyberLeek, the group behind the alleged Grand Theft Auto 6 Xbox dump, released a 57 MB executable on November 23, 2026, and modders have already started picking at it, according to LevelUp’s report on the GTA 6 executable leak . The headline sounds like a finish line. It is closer to a starting gun.
The file comes from an Xbox Series X|S build, not from any official PC release, and a CyberLeek administrator has already said in plain terms that it does not run the game. This article sorts what outlets have actually reported from what forum threads and social posts are promising. It follows our earlier piece on the five CyberLeek claims and the one missing file , which flagged exactly this gap.
Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google
Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions.
Here is the short version. Reports say CyberLeek published the executable tied to the leaked Xbox build on November 23, 2026. That executable reportedly matches version 1.0.2.1 of the Xbox Series X|S build, and the archive that carries it weighs 57 MB.
The leak does not stand alone. An earlier alleged dump of the same build circulated as a 209 GB torrent. Per the reporting, that torrent held files for Rockstar’s RAGE game engine and for the Xbox console. What it lacked was the executable, the small program that ties those files together and tells the hardware what to do with them.
Coverage has come from several named outlets. LevelUp, eTeknix, ShiftDelete.Net and TechJuice all ran the story, and the outlets we can link to directly include GamesIndustry.biz, which framed it as a leaker reportedly releasing the file needed to run the leaked Xbox build . The word “reportedly” appears in that headline for a reason. Nobody outside the leak community has confirmed that the files are authentic or complete.
The core point for readers is simple. A leaked executable does not equal a playable game. It is one missing piece in a pile that still has plenty of missing pieces.
Size comparisons make this story look lopsided. The archive is 57 MB, while the earlier alleged dump ran to 209 GB. Yet the small file is the one that modders had been waiting for. We said as much when the dump first surfaced, in our look at how PC port hopes hinged on one missing file in 209 GB .
Think of the dump as a warehouse of parts and the executable as the assembly instructions. Game assets, engine files and console components tell you what the game contains. The executable tells you how the pieces connect and what code runs when the game starts. Without it, a port team can study the parts but cannot easily see how the machine fits together.
That explains why outlets treated the release as a development worth reporting. PCMag had earlier covered the saga under the headline GTA 6 leaker releases all files for alleged Xbox build of game , and the new archive extends that story rather than replacing it.
It also explains why the number 57 matters less than the version label. Version 1.0.2.1 gives modders a fixed target. When a community works from one specific build, people can compare notes, share findings and avoid chasing mismatched files. That coordination is often what turns a scattered hobby into a real project.
The most important sentence in this story came from CyberLeek itself. Coverage of the release quotes an unnamed CyberLeek administrator as writing: “This .exe file does NOT RUN THE GAME.” That is about as direct as a leaker gets.
The same administrator reportedly set expectations on timing too. The reported line reads: “It will take at least a week for us to get somewhere noticeable to the point where you can play on your pc.” Two details stand out. The group says “at least,” which makes a week a floor and not a promise. And “noticeable” is a modest target, well short of “finished” or even “stable.”
Some social posts have run ahead of that. One claim says a playable PC version will arrive within days. Reports do not confirm it, and it conflicts with the administrator’s own estimate. Another claim says modders have already built a playable PC version. The reporting says the opposite, describing a build that stays unplayable or only partly boots.
Why does a console executable not simply run on a Windows machine? Because it was compiled for different hardware, different system libraries and a different operating environment. The code expects an Xbox to be underneath it. A PC is not an X

articles.t: GTA 6 : le hacker qui avait piraté Rockstar condamné à sept ans de prison à 21 ans
articles.chapeau: Arion Kurtaj, 21 ans, le hacker qui avait fait fuiter GTA 6 avant sa sortie, est condamné à sept ans de prison à Londres. On refait l'histoire.
articles.txt:
Il n’avait pas encore 20 ans quand il a mis Rockstar Games à genoux. Aujourd’hui, la justice britannique vient de lui présenter l’addition.
Arion Kurtaj, le jeune hacker derrière la fuite massive de GTA 6, est condamné à sept ans de prison à Londres. Retour sur un dossier qui a secoué l’industrie du jeu vidéo.
Tout commence en septembre 2022. Des dizaines de vidéos de gameplay de GTA 6, encore en plein développement, apparaissent sur un forum. Les images sont brutes, inachevées, mais bien réelles.
Les fans n’en reviennent pas. Rockstar, lui, est en état de choc. Le studio confirme l’intrusion dans ses systèmes et parle d’une attaque informatique majeure, sans précédent pour la franchise.
Ces images avaient d’ailleurs déclenché une vague de panique chez l’éditeur, qui avait riposté en justice. On vous avait raconté cette fuite de gameplay qui a fait paniquer Rockstar à l’époque.
Mais derrière l’écran, qui tapait sur le clavier ? La réponse a surpris tout le monde.
Le profil du pirate détonne. Arion Kurtaj était alors un adolescent, à peine majeur. Il agissait, selon l’enquête, au sein du groupe Lapsus$, une bande connue pour s’attaquer à de grandes entreprises.
Le groupe ne visait pas que Rockstar. Plusieurs géants de la tech et du jeu vidéo avaient déjà été touchés avant lui.
Le plus troublant, c’est la méthode. Pas de super-virus ni de code ultra-sophistiqué ici, mais de l’ingénierie sociale, c’est-à-dire l’art de manipuler des humains pour obtenir des accès.
Et le jeune hacker ne s’est pas arrêté là. Ce qu’il a fait ensuite a précipité sa chute.
Arrêté une première fois, il avait été remis en liberté. Mais l’histoire ne s’est pas arrêtée là : il a continué à sévir malgré la surveillance de la police.
Les enquêteurs ont fini par rassembler assez d’éléments pour le traduire en justice. Verdict final : sept ans de prison. À 21 ans, il va donc passer une bonne partie de sa jeunesse derrière les barreaux.
La peine est lourde, surtout au regard de son âge. Elle envoie un message clair à tous ceux qui seraient tentés de jouer aux apprentis pirates avec les géants du secteur.
L’ironie de l’histoire, c’est que la fuite n’a pas freiné le jeu. Au contraire. Rockstar a repris la main, et GTA VI est bel et bien sorti à la date prévue, le 19 novembre 2026 .
Résultat : un succès record, déjà largement commenté chez nous. Les joueurs se sont rués sur le titre, au point d’en faire l’un des lancements les plus attendus de l’histoire du jeu vidéo.
Avant même la sortie, la hype était telle que les fans s’organisaient pour dénicher le meilleur prix et poser leurs congés.
Les fuites, elles, n’ont pas disparu pour autant. D’autres leakers continuent de rôder, comme celui qui avait parié sur la date du trailer 3 , avec des infos qui s’étaient révélées exactes.
Cette condamnation rappelle une réalité : le jeu vidéo est devenu une cible de choix. Des budgets colossaux, des communautés ultra-actives, des secrets industriels à fort enjeu.
Pour les studios, la sécurité n’est plus une option. Un seul employé piégé peut suffire à ouvrir la porte à des pirates, même très jeunes.
Quant à Arion Kurtaj, son nom restera associé à l’une des plus grosses fuites de l’histoire du secteur. Pas vraiment le genre de trophée dont on rêve à 21 ans.
Reste une question : d’autres membres du groupe seront-ils rattrapés à leur tour ? Les enquêtes se poursuivent, et la justice semble déterminée à aller jusqu’au bout.
En attendant, les joueurs, eux, peuvent profiter du jeu sans avoir à se demander ce qui se passait en coulisses. Et si vous cherchez la suite de l’actu, jetez un œil à cette carte deux fois plus grande que celle de GTA 5 .

articles.t: Hacker Who Leaked GTA 6 Footage Sentenced to Seven Years in Prison but Immediately Released
articles.chapeau: 21-year-old Arion Kurtaj has been sentenced to seven years in prison for a series of cyberattacks, including the Rockstar Games hack and the leak of 90 videos from an early version of GTA 6. However, he was released on licence that same day because the court took into account the time he had already spent in custody and in a specialist hospital, the BBC reports.
articles.txt:
Yevgeny Demkivskyi Author of news at Mezha and a geek. I write about technology, movies, and games. Perhaps with a little more passion for games. 24 November, 16:53 0 21-year-old Arion Kurtaj has been sentenced to seven years in prison for a series of cyberattacks, including the Rockstar Games hack and the leak of 90 videos from an early version of GTA 6. However, he was released on licence that same day because the court took into account the time he had already spent in custody and in a specialist hospital, the BBC reports .
Release on licence does not overturn the sentence. Kurtaj will serve the remainder of his sentence outside prison but must comply with the conditions imposed on him. If he breaches those conditions, he could be returned to prison.
The court initially determined a nine-year sentence but reduced it by two years to account for the time Kurtaj had spent in hospital under a court order. The hacker was arrested and taken into custody back in September 2022. In 2023, he was placed under an indefinite hospital order because he was unable to participate fully in court proceedings.
In January 2026, the hospital order was lifted, after which Kurtaj was transferred to a regular prison and preparations began for a new hearing. A week before sentencing, he pleaded guilty to six charges: one count of fraud, four offences under the UK's Computer Misuse Act, and one count of unlawfully possessing a mobile phone in prison. Seven further charges were left on file without being heard.
Kurtaj was a member of the Lapsus$ group and attacked Rockstar Games in September 2022 while already on bail for other cybercrimes. Using the alias TeaPotUberHacker, he published nearly an hour of footage from the unfinished GTA 6 and threatened to release the game's source code. Rockstar estimated that recovering from the attack cost the company approximately $5 million and thousands of hours of employee work.
The sentence also covers attacks on telecommunications companies BT and EE, fintech service Revolut, and Uber. During the Uber hack, Kurtaj stole internal data and deleted some information and accounts, causing the company more than $2.8 million in losses. The attack on Revolut compromised the data of thousands of users.
According to the BBC, Kurtaj's online activity will be restricted for the next five years under a separate Serious Crime Prevention Order. In particular, he will be prohibited from using Telegram and Discord. The judge described Kurtaj as a talented young man and warned him: "Don't do it again."
